answer_core:
I would not choose the advisor's hybrid direction yet. I would run a two-week constraint test first: get your advisor's permission to explore it, ask Dr. Silva for a concrete data/collaboration reality check, and ask what role would actually be available if this became a dissertation path.

The key condition is not whether option 3 is intellectually exciting. It is whether the fallback stays real. Do not design an 18-month pivot unless option 1, or a modified version of it, will still have supervision, funding, and enough lab continuity when that trigger fires. If your advisor cannot explicitly protect that fallback, the trigger is fake comfort.

Use Dr. Silva as a constraint test, not as a hopeful name. Option 3 only becomes viable if usable data, sharing terms, and collaborator depth are concrete enough to carry dissertation risk. Keep broad success-rate talk qualitative unless you find a real reference class for similar dissertations under similar lab and advisor constraints.

So the next move is advisor first, Silva second, committee third. After those probes, choose the path that keeps you finishing a PhD real, not the path that only looks best in an abstract field map.
